messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: ACME MAP - POC environment dependencies & next steps

Hi Jordan / Sam,

Thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap and the draft MAP milestone for the POC environment setup so we can align on owners and target dates. I've attached an editable milestones spreadsheet and our network checklist.

Summary of dependencies we discussed (POC env):
- VPC peering and route table setup (required for API traffic) - target: 2 business days after acceptance
- IP allowlist (static egress IPs) - ACME to provide desired CIDR ranges; Redwood to confirm final egress IPs
- SSO / SAML integration for admin access (Okta) - SSO metadata exchange + test user required
- Secrets / KMS access for model keys (customer-managed KMS option) - procurement of service principal and KMS grant

Draft MAP milestone (high level):
- Milestone: POC environment provisioning complete
  - Owner: ACME infra (VPC peering, allowlist) + Redwood infra (routing, NAT, firewall)
  - Deliverables: Peering up, allowlist confirmed, SSO test user, secrets grant configured
  - Target completion: 2026-07-23 (we can adjust based on your internal approvals)
  - Dependencies: ACME security sign-off on egress IPs, Okta admin time to exchange metadata, KMS grant approval from your security team

Action items / next steps:
1) Jordan / Sam: Can you confirm the ACME owners for VPC peering and KMS and reasonable target dates for each item?
2) Nikhil: I've assigned you on the MAP to coordinate the SSO and network test plan. Please confirm availability for a 30-min runbook walk-through Friday.
3) Jordan: Please review the attached milestones sheet and add any internal SLAs/approval steps you need.

Attachments:
- acme-map-milestones.xlsx (editable)
- redwood-poc-network-checklist.pdf (network checklist)

If this looks good I'll update the MAP in HubSpot and propose the canary rollout window for the week after we go green on the environment.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Marissa,

Thanks for the clear summary. Quick answers and notes from our side:

VPC peering / routing: Owner: Samantha Lee (cc'd). We can get the peering request raised tomorrow (7/17). Expect routing + security review by 7/19. We use AWS in us-west-2.

IP allowlist: We're still finalizing outbound proxy ranges with our NetOps team - earliest we can confirm is 7/18. If Redwood can provide the list of egress IPs you need for the POC, that will speed things up.

SSO / SAML (Okta): Owner: Jordan Bell. I can get Okta metadata to you by EOD 7/16 and can create a test admin user. We may need Redwood to validate assertion consumer service (ACS) URL and entity ID.

KMS / secrets: Owner: Security (I'll loop in them after this email). We prefer customer-managed KMS; I think we can schedule the grant request for 7/19 once peering is approved.

Attachments: I uploaded an internal network diagram to the shared Drive folder you linked and added a couple of notes to the milestone sheet (ACME internal approval steps).

Questions for Redwood:
- Can you confirm whether the POC will require persistent data storage or ephemeral caches only? (affects KMS scope)
- Do you support SAML attribute mappings for role-based admin access? We'd like to provision both admin and observer roles.

We're aligned on the target week of 7/23 but will update if any approvals slip.

Thanks,

Jordan Bell
Senior Cloud Engineer, ACME Corp
jordan.bell@acme.com | +1 206-555-0199

Date: Fri, 17 Jul 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME MAP - POC environment dependencies & next steps

Jordan / Sam,

Thanks for the updates and for uploading the notes. Quick operational responses from the infra side:

- Egress IPs: For the POC we can operate with a small fixed pool. I'll share the list of Redwood egress IPs by EOD 7/17. Those are the IPs to add to your allowlist.
- Persistent storage: The POC uses ephemeral caches for inference; no persistent customer data will be written to long-term storage unless you opt into session logs. If you require persistence we can enable and scope KMS access accordingly.
- SAML attributes / RBAC: We support SAML attribute mapping; we typically map groups to two roles (admin / observer) and can share the attribute mapping doc. I'll also schedule a 30-min SSO walk-through for Friday 7/17 at 11:00 PT (inv coming).
- KMS grant flow: For customer-managed KMS we require a service principal with a GrantToAllowEncryptDecrypt policy. Security will need to approve; happy to provide the exact IAM/KMS policy snippet for your team.

Next steps:
- Jordan: confirm owners for KMS approval (security contact) and confirm final allowlist by 7/18.
- Samantha: please confirm peering ticket when created so I can watch it and test routing once it's up.
- Marissa / I: we'll upload the final MAP to HubSpot after Jordan confirms allowlist.

Attachments referenced: redwood-poc-network-checklist.pdf (network checklist), acme-map-milestones.xlsx (updated with ACME notes).

Thanks,

Nikhil Sharma
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
nikhil.sharma@redwood.com | +1 650-555-0098
